page.layout: Running head at top centre; page number at top right; one column of running text, full width; catchword at right below the last line; signature at the foot. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: melius est vt vendatur Hismaelitis,& manus nostræ non polluantur: frater.n. & caro nostra est. Ita Dauid,Ecce quàm bonū & quàm iucundū,habitare fratres in vnū. Sicut oleū preciosum super caput, quod descēdit in barbam Aaron, quod descendit in oræ vestimenti eius. Sicut ros Hermon qui descendit in montem Sion: Quoniam illic promisit Dominus benedictionē, & vitam vsq; in seculū. Ita Paulus, Obsecro vos fratres, per nomen [?] Domini nostri Iesu Christi,vt idē loquamini omnes,& non sint inter vos dissidia,sed sitis integrum corpus, eadē mente & eadem sententia. Sic Petrus: In pietate aut [?] subministrate [?] fraternam charitatem. Et Ioannes,Nos scimus quòd translati sumus de morte ad vitā, quia diligimus fratres. Qui nō diligit fratre, manet in morte. Omnis qui odit fratrem suum, homicida est. Et scitis quòd omnis homicida non habet vitam æternam in se manentem. Per hoc cognouimus charitatem,quoniam ille animam suam pro nobis posuit, & nos debemus pro fratribus animas ponere. Hæc etsi de omnibus Christianis & spiritualibus fratribus dicta sunt: tamen etiam ad naturales fratres referri possunt ac debent. Est autem fratrū inter se concordia (vt Antisthenes dixit) quouis muro firmius munimentum.
Secundum, quod pulchrum est, & Deo ac hominibus placet, est φιλία πλησίων [?], i. amor proximorum, dum ciues & vicini mutuum sibi diligunt: erunt enim ciuitas firma.

page.notes: The catchword "Ac" stands at the right edge, on the same line as "firma.", and is taken as the catchword of the next page. The Greek phrase after "est" is only partly legible; the second word is doubtful. Long s is printed as f in "Hifmaelitis", "fubminiftra" and "dissidia"; these are read as s. The running head is read as "NVPTIALES." and corrected to NUPTIALES. The page number at top right is partly unclear. The Latin "aut" and "subministrate" are uncertain because of the broken line. The word "per nomen" is blurred at the line break.
